persona_summary.name: Surgical Regression Test — Container Resize
persona_summary.archetype: Targeted scenario: one parent container, one child node
persona_summary.test_focus: Validate the exact defect: a container with a node in it cannot be expanded or shrunk

executive_summary.verdict: CONFIRMED BUG — container resize is completely non-functional when the container has child nodes
executive_summary.expand_result: FAIL — node.style('width/height') is stored but the Cytoscape compound node bounding box stays fixed at the children-driven size (113x115.5 regardless of style value from 99px to 300px)
executive_summary.shrink_result: FAIL — same root cause; min-size clamping to 99px works correctly but the visual BB is unaffected
executive_summary.secondary_bug: FAIL — the invalid/clamped style value (99px) is autosaved to the database and persists after page reload, creating a permanent style/visual mismatch
executive_summary.root_cause: Cytoscape.js compound node (isParent=true) bounding box is always computed from the union of children bounding boxes + padding. Setting node.style('width') or node.style('height') on a compound node with children has NO visual effect — the style is stored but never reflected in the rendered BB. The resize bridge (_htResizeApply) applies the correct style values but they are silently ignored by Cytoscape for parent nodes.
executive_summary.scope: ALL containers with children. Empty containers are unaffected (style width/height works when there are no children).
executive_summary.fix_direction: The resize bridge must move/offset child nodes when the container is expanded/shrunk, not just set the container style. Expand: offset each child by deltaW/2, deltaH/2 away from center. Shrink: clamp based on children BB + padding, then offset children inward.

prioritized_issues.title: Container resize handles are completely non-functional when container has child nodes
prioritized_issues.action: Drag resize handle (SE corner or any edge) of a container that has at least one child node
prioritized_issues.steps_to_reproduce: 1. Create a topology in edit mode. 2. Drop a Server node and publish it to inventory. 3. Right-click → 'Convert to Container'. 4. Drop a second Server node, publish it, then move it inside the container (compound parent relationship). 5. Click the container to select it — resize handles appear. 6. Drag the SE handle outward to expand or inward to shrink. 7. Release. Expected: container grows or shrinks. Actual: container size is completely unchanged.

expand_test.position_drift: Container center shifted ~10px due to node.position() call on compound node — unintended side effect
expand_test.style_after_reload: 99px (from shrink test autosave) — container renders at 113 but style is 99

direct_api_test.bounding_box_after: 113 × 115.5 — STYLE IGNORED BY CYTOSCAPE FOR COMPOUND NODES WITH CHILDREN

prioritized_issues.title: Failed container resize autosaves corrupted style value (99px) that persists after reload
prioritized_issues.action: Drag shrink handle on container with child → autosave fires → reload page
prioritized_issues.steps_to_reproduce: 1. Reproduce issue #1 shrink test. 2. Wait ~1 second (autosave schedules at 800ms). 3. Press F5 / navigate away and back to the topology. 4. Inspect: container.style('width') = '99px' but container.boundingBox().w = 113.

evidence.mismatch: Style declares 99px min but container visually renders at 113px — permanent silent mismatch in saved state
evidence.impact: Any downstream consumer of the style property (export, thumbnails, snapshots) sees 99px rather than the true 113px

prioritized_issues.title: Container center position drifts on resize attempt — node.position() side-effect on compound nodes
prioritized_issues.action: Resize handle drag on container with children
prioritized_issues.steps_to_reproduce: 1. Note container position (x1, y1). 2. Drag SE handle to expand. 3. Observe: BB x1/y1 shifts by ~10px (the signX * deltaW/2 position offset from _htResizeApply), even though the size didn't change.

evidence.cause: _htResizeApply calls node.position(calc.position) which DOES move the compound center for compound nodes, even though node.style('width/height') has no effect. This causes unintended container drift with every resize attempt.

technical_analysis.root_cause_detail: Cytoscape.js compound node (isParent() === true) bounding box is computed dynamically from the union of its children's bounding boxes, expanded by the compound's padding. The `node.style('width')` and `node.style('height')` properties on a compound node with children only declare a minimum — but since the children's BB + padding (99px) is smaller than the children-driven actual size (113px), the minimum never triggers. More critically: even setting style to 300px (>> 113px) did not change the bounding box, indicating that Cytoscape does NOT recalculate compound size from style when children are present. The computed size is frozen at the children-union size.
technical_analysis.why_position_works_but_size_doesnt: node.position({x, y}) on a compound node moves the geometric center of the compound AND all its children together. This is why position drift occurs. But node.style('width/height') for compound nodes is rendered as a style hint that Cytoscape evaluates ONLY when the compound has no children or when layout recalculates.

fix_approach.expand: When expanding, compute the delta per side (e.g., delta/2 on each axis for SE drag). Then offset each child node position by that delta away from the container center. The compound node's BB will grow naturally as children move outward.
fix_approach.shrink: When shrinking, clamp so that new size >= children_BB + padding. Then offset each child node position inward by the same delta. The compound BB will shrink as children move inward.
fix_approach.code_location: _htResizeApply in canvas_js_resize.py needs to be updated to handle compound nodes (node.isParent()) differently from leaf nodes.
